content:
The market generally expects Apple to launch a brand-new OLED iPad mini as early as the end of this month. Today, an unverified new rumour once again claims that the new iPad mini will switch to an OLED display, but will still maintain a 60Hz refresh rate and will not support ProMotion.

The OLED iPad mini may not feature ProMotion

This is already the second time we have heard this rumour, but both times come from the same source: the yeux1122 account on Naver. That account has a very mixed track record for Apple rumours, and often appears to just be relaying messages from unknown origins rather than providing exclusive information itself.

However, yeux1122's latest post claims that some 'overseas sources' mention the new OLED iPad mini will have 120Hz, but that 'domestic production numbers have already been confirmed' to use a 60Hz display.

I remain highly sceptical of this rumour, as no other reliable sources have corroborated it so far.

Nevertheless, if the rumour is true, it would be a disappointing shortcoming for iPad mini buyers. This iPad mini upgrade is expected to bring several other notable improvements, including:

  • An OLED display.
  • An Apple A20 Pro chip, an upgrade over the A17 Pro chip in the current iPad mini.
  • A redesigned exterior with thinner bezels, and potentially improved water resistance.
  • The FaceTime camera will move to the landscape edge, aligning with Apple's other iPad models.

If Apple implements all of the above changes but holds back on the display, failing to upgrade to ProMotion with a 120Hz refresh rate, it would significantly diminish the debut of the new iPad mini.

The new iPad mini is expected to be announced at the end of this month, so we won't have to wait long to find out.

What do you think? Will the new iPad mini feature ProMotion and a 120Hz refresh rate? Let us know in the comments.
